headline: Highest risk is data leakage: next-ai-draw-io uses broad network/MCP and API keys, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list with no shared channel, so other risks are mostly limited by missing interaction surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, while next-ai-draw-io has browser/MCP tooling but no documented bridge from the list into its instruction stream. With no shared channel or ingestion path shown, prompt injection between the pair is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF awesome-selfhosted content is pasted into next-ai-draw-io as trusted instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Treat any copied text from awesome-selfhosted as untrusted input.
Disable MCP routes that can ingest arbitrary external text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and broad network egress, so if it receives sensitive files from awesome-selfhosted’s workspace or copied content, leakage can occur through third-party APIs. awesome-selfhosted itself shows no data handling, so the risk is driven by B’s outbound surfaces rather than A.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are opened in next-ai-draw-io, they may be sent to external model APIs.
IF the two agents share a workspace or clipboard, copied content can flow from A-associated material into B's outbound requests.
mitigations: Avoid loading sensitive files into next-ai-draw-io.
Use a local-only model backend where possible.
Rotate or scope API keys before testing.
Separate workspaces and disable shared clipboard.
requires-engineering: enforce outbound allowlists and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally with next-ai-draw-io’s browser/MCP and API usage. The only overlap is conceptual content, not shared writes or locks, making capability conflict minimal.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator gives them shared mutable OAuth scopes, overlapping writes become possible.
mitigations: Keep A read-only and non-runnable.
Do not grant B write access to shared repos unless necessary.
Use separate credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can turn inputs into diagrams and actions via browser/MCP workflows, so if it consumes content derived from awesome-selfhosted without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. A is a static list, but B’s natural-language command flow makes unverified propagation plausible.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io treats imported text from awesome-selfhosted as authoritative, mistakes can propagate.
IF B is used to generate deliverables or trigger browser actions from A-derived content, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before exporting diagrams.
Cross-check imported facts against source URLs.
Use a verification checklist for AI-generated edits.
Separate source notes from generated output.
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and sends content to multiple external AI providers, while awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge list with no compliance controls shown. If regulated or confidential material is processed in B, residency and retention obligations may be harder to satisfy; A is not the compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through next-ai-draw-io, external API routing may create residency or retention issues.
IF organizational policy forbids third-party model processing, B’s default API integrations conflict with that policy.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in B.
Use a self-hosted/local model endpoint.
Review API-provider retention settings.
Store API keys in a dedicated secret manager.
requires-engineering: document DPA/residency controls per provider.
